findings.body: In Ruby the later definition (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) overrides the earlier (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) one, so calls passing four dimension args plus opts raise ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4), breaking emoji resizing.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime ArgumentError on existing five-argument downsize callers.
findings.impact: In Ruby the later definition (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) overrides the earlier (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) one, so calls passing four dimension args plus opts raise ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4), breaking emoji resizing.
findings.root_cause: A new self.downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts) was added without removing the existing self.downsize(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts), creating a method redefinition.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not define two methods named downsize; keep only one signature (either accept dimensions string, updating resize_emoji to pass a single dimensions arg, or keep the 4-arg version) so all existing callers remain valid.
findings.title: Duplicate downsize method shadows 4-argument version, breaking resize_emoji
findings.trigger: Any call to OptimizedImage.downsize with five arguments, e.g. app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb calling OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts).
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 without removing the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. In Ruby, the later definition shadows the earlier one. Repository context shows `resize_emoji.rb:14` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments, which will now fail with ArgumentError since only the 3-4 argument version remains visible.

raw_findings.body: The download cap ignores the site setting, always allowing up to 10MB regardless of the administrator-configured limit, so remote files far larger than the configured maximum are fetched.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Behavioral divergence from administrator configuration for API URL uploads.
raw_findings.impact: The download cap ignores the site setting, always allowing up to 10MB regardless of the administrator-configured limit, so remote files far larger than the configured maximum are fetched.
raw_findings.root_cause: Configured site-setting-based size limit was replaced with a hardcoded constant.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes (or the appropriate per-type setting) as the download size limit instead of the hardcoded 10.megabytes.
raw_findings.title: API upload download size hardcoded to 10MB instead of configured max_image_size_kb
raw_findings.trigger: An API client submits a URL upload for a site where max_image_size_kb is configured to something other than 10240 KB (default is 3072).

raw_findings.body: Client-side validation no longer honors the configured max_'+type+'_size_kb setting nor distinguishes image vs attachment limits, so oversized (up to 10MB) files pass client validation and are only rejected later by the server, and the error dialog reports 10240 KB rather than the real limit.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Client validation diverges from server limits, giving misleading messages and deferring rejection.
raw_findings.impact: Client-side validation no longer honors the configured max_'+type+'_size_kb setting nor distinguishes image vs attachment limits, so oversized (up to 10MB) files pass client validation and are only rejected later by the server, and the error dialog reports 10240 KB rather than the real limit.
raw_findings.root_cause: Site-setting-based per-type limit was replaced by a hardcoded constant.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore var maxSizeKB = Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']; so the client uses the per-type configured limit.
raw_findings.title: Client upload size check hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring per-type site setting
raw_findings.trigger: A user uploads an attachment (type='attachment') or an image on a site where max_attachment_size_kb / max_image_size_kb differs from 10240 KB (defaults are 3072).

raw_findings.body: The 'file too large' dialog displays 10240 KB as the maximum regardless of the actual configured limit, misinforming the user.
raw_findings.impact: The 'file too large' dialog displays 10240 KB as the maximum regardless of the actual configured limit, misinforming the user.
raw_findings.root_cause: Site-setting-based value was replaced by a hardcoded constant in the 413 handler.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore var maxSizeKB = Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb; so the displayed limit matches configuration.
raw_findings.title: 413 error dialog max size hardcoded to 10MB instead of site setting
raw_findings.trigger: The web server returns HTTP 413 for an oversized upload on a site whose max_image_size_kb differs from 10240 KB.

raw_findings.body: The loop may read a stale size and either exit early (leaving an oversized file) or continue unnecessarily, and Upload.create_for is later given a possibly stale tempfile.size.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Possible incorrect size comparison after external rewrite.
raw_findings.impact: The loop may read a stale size and either exit early (leaving an oversized file) or continue unnecessarily, and Upload.create_for is later given a possibly stale tempfile.size.
raw_findings.root_cause: New loop assumes Tempfile#size reflects modifications made by an external process to the same path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Re-stat the path explicitly (e.g., File.size(tempfile.path)) inside the loop and when passing size to Upload.create_for to ensure the current on-disk size is used.
raw_findings.title: Downsize loop relies on tempfile.size that may not reflect externally-rewritten file
raw_findings.trigger: A large image is downsized via OptimizedImage.downsize (which runs an external convert process writing to tempfile.path); if convert replaces the inode via rename, the open Tempfile descriptor's cached stat may not reflect the new file size.

finding.failure_mode: Possible incorrect size comparison after external rewrite.
finding.impact: The loop may read a stale size and either exit early (leaving an oversized file) or continue unnecessarily, and Upload.create_for is later given a possibly stale tempfile.size.
finding.root_cause: New loop assumes Tempfile#size reflects modifications made by an external process to the same path.

finding.title: Downsize loop relies on tempfile.size that may not reflect externally-rewritten file
finding.trigger: A large image is downsized via OptimizedImage.downsize (which runs an external convert process writing to tempfile.path); if convert replaces the inode via rename, the open Tempfile descriptor's cached stat may not reflect the new file size.
finding.verifier_reason: This is speculative. The claim that Tempfile#size may be stale after external process writes is not substantiated by the patch. Ruby's Tempfile wraps a File object and File#size performs a stat call. The patch introduces the loop but the candidate provides no concrete evidence that ImageMagick's convert replaces the inode via rename or that stat caching occurs. The impact is hypothetical without proof.
